page: Amazon Web Services c7gn.metal is a bare-metal, compute-optimized server powered by 64 dedicated physical cores of the ARMv8-based AWS Graviton Neoverse-V1 processor. Operating at a clock speed of 2.6 GHz, this arm64 architecture features 64 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache per core, and a shared 32 MB L3 cache. The system is equipped with 128.0 GB of DDR5 memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or GPU hardware, relying instead on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 200 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core capabilities and memory performance. The server achieved a top-tier rating in the Geekbench multi-core test with a score of 20,886.0 and in software compilation using Clang with a score of 59,675.0. Memory performance is highly efficient, with Passmark memory scores in the top tier and uncached large-block read bandwidth reaching 277.09 GB/sec. Multi-core CPU performance via stress-ng is rated as strong at 98,074.28, while single-core performance across stress-ng and Geekbench remains in the average tier.

Given its high-bandwidth networking and strong multi-threaded execution, the c7gn.metal is well-suited for network-intensive compute workloads, software compilation, database operations, and static web serving. It demonstrates strong performance in Redis SET operations, executing 101.71 million operations per second. However, the lack of local NVMe storage and dedicated GPU accelerators makes it less suitable for local-storage-heavy databases or high-end GPU-accelerated deep learning, though it maintains average efficiency for CPU-based LLM prompt processing.
